bullets.title: Fed holds with 23-33% surprise hike odds; Warsh messaging is the key watch
bullets.body: Kalshi traders assign 77% probability to a hold and 23% to a surprise 25bp hike; CME FedWatch shows 24% vs. SOFR-implied 32%, which one analyst calls 'historically anomalous one day before a meeting.' Ned Davis Research says traders underestimate hike risk and expects a very close vote; all focus is on Chair Warsh's post-decision messaging for September clues.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector down 22.5% in July — worst month since December 2002
bullets.body: Chip stocks are on track for their worst monthly decline since 2002, with a head-and-shoulders pattern nearly complete at the ~528 neckline. Hedge funds dumped global tech at the fastest pace in nearly two years on Friday; July 2026 is shaping up as the worst momentum month on record (ex-COVID). BTIG warns against pressing shorts at current levels.

bullets.title: Market overreacting to hyperscale credit-spread widening, says Gavin Baker
bullets.body: Gavin Baker argues the market is misreading hyperscale credit spread widening: GPU spot pricing significantly exceeds contracted rates, suggesting hyperscalers are underearning, and accelerating operating cash flow is an underestimated funding source for AI capex. Multiple accounts RT'd the view, calling the AI infrastructure sell-off overdone.

bullets.title: META on 9-day losing streak — longest in company history
bullets.body: META has declined for nine consecutive trading sessions, its longest streak ever. Zuckerberg was active on X/WSJ arguing the US should accelerate—not restrict—AI development and opposing a ban on Chinese AI, framing open competition as the better policy path.

bullets.title: TSLA most oversold since March 2025; Musk companies lose $1.5T combined since mid-June
bullets.body: Tesla has fallen to its most oversold RSI level since March 2025. Elon Musk's companies (Tesla + SpaceX) have shed a combined $1.5T in value since mid-June per one account. Elon separately reaffirmed that supervised FSD 'unequivocally saves lives' and that regulatory delays cost lives.

bullets.title: INTC down 23% since Cramer's call; BofA reiterates Buy at $160 PT
bullets.body: INTC has lost $130B in market cap since Jim Cramer said 'Intel's the one.' Despite the drawdown, BofA reiterated Buy with a $160 PT after an IR call citing server business inflection and growing foundry visibility. Separately, Intel Foundry disclosed a blueprint for hyper-large form factor chip packages with a void-free encapsulation process, and an $8.8M institutional call sweep was flagged.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Q2 miss read as overblown; AI memory cycle broadening beyond HBM
bullets.body: SK Hynix missed Q2 revenue ($54.6B vs $57.7B est) and operating profit ($60.5T won vs $64.2T won est) but net income beat ($93.8T won vs $54.3T won). One analyst with a +150% PT called the miss 'overblown' and attributed it to HBM product mix, not supercycle weakness. SK Hynix flagged broadening AI demand into conventional server DRAM, enterprise SSDs, and networking, with HBM4 shipments expected to lift H2 ASPs.

bullets.title: Credo (CRDO) sold off on market misread of Jensen's 'cableless' comment
bullets.body: One semiconductor analyst explains Jensen Huang's 'cableless' remark referred to internal GPU-to-GPU cabling replaced by midplane PCB assembly—not external-to-rack cabling. Credo makes external-to-rack cables and is unaffected; Nvidia telegraphed this design change months ago. The selloff was characterized as a market misunderstanding.

bullets.title: NVDA Taiwan office raided in Super Micro AI server smuggling case
bullets.body: Taiwanese prosecutors raided Nvidia's Taiwan office and an employee's home as part of a case involving the alleged smuggling of high-end Super Micro Computer AI servers to China in violation of export controls. One Nvidia employee was detained as the prime suspect.

bullets.title: Bloom Energy (BE) raises FY revenue guidance to $3.9-4.2B; stock up 10% AH
bullets.body: Bloom Energy posted an earnings 'triple play' after the close—raising full-year revenue guidance from $3.4-3.8B to $3.9-4.2B, well above the Bloomberg consensus of $3.74B. CEO cited conversations with all major US hyperscalers and a dozen neo-cloud providers as evidence of BTM infrastructure demand acceleration from AI. Stock up 10% AH despite being down 11% intraday and ~39% from June highs.

bullets.title: Seagate (STX) strong Q4 beat; Q1 guidance far above consensus on cloud demand
bullets.body: STX Q4 revenue $3.63B (+48% YoY) beat the $3.49B consensus; adjusted EPS $5.71 vs. $5.08 est. Q1 guidance of $4.0-4.2B revenue and $7.10-7.50 EPS both blew past estimates of $3.75B and $5.80. Management cited robust cloud data center demand and expects durable long-term mass-capacity storage demand into 2027.

bullets.title: KLA Corp (KLAC) down ~10% AH; share-gain commentary warns against undifferentiated process-control basket
bullets.body: KLA beat Q4 revenue estimates but dropped ~10% after hours. One analyst highlighted KLA's share-gain commentary as a warning not to treat process-control companies (ONTO, CAMT, NVMI, AMAT, ASML) as an undifferentiated basket—differentiation within the group matters.

bullets.title: Marvell optical engineering SVP proposes alternative to large campus data center build
bullets.body: A contact from Marvell's optical engineering team (SVP/CTO level) shared a perspective favoring distributed interconnect/networking solutions over large-campus data center consolidation, positioning it as an alternative architecture for AI infrastructure scaling.

bullets.title: ANET, AVGO, MRVL, VRT: multi-year AI data-center storage allocations extend infrastructure spend duration
bullets.body: A semiconductor/infrastructure analyst argues that multi-year storage allocations in AI data centers are extending the duration of capex cycles, supporting sustained demand for networking, semiconductor, and power infrastructure providers including Arista, Broadcom, Marvell, and Vertiv.

bullets.title: PLTR previewed for strong 2Q26 growth on broad government demand
bullets.body: An analyst preview expects Palantir to maintain strong growth momentum in Q2 2026, driven by broad-based government demand across U.S. defense, civilian federal agencies, and international government customers. One fintwit account separately called PLTR 'still sucks.'

bullets.title: GLW (Corning) posts strong quarter; Enterprise sales +65% YoY, Gen AI products nearly doubled
bullets.body: Corning reported very strong results with Enterprise sales reaching $1.27B (+65% YoY) and Gen AI product revenue nearly doubling. Management tone described as notably enthusiastic; AI-data-center portion of Enterprise segment was the key driver.

bullets.title: AAPL, ABNB hit 52-week highs; tech sees rotation as GOOGL, SHOP, MDB held
bullets.body: AAPL and ABNB reached new 52-week highs on Tuesday. One fintwit account said it is 'starting to get interested in tech stocks again,' holding SHOP and MDB and eyeing GOOGL and ARM for new positions. AAPL separately preparing a new smart home push built around an updated Siri AI hub device.

bullets.title: MU: $3M+ OTM call sweep and bullish read-through from SK Hynix memory commentary
bullets.body: Unusual Whales flagged $3M+ in out-of-the-money Micron call options as unusual institutional activity. Separately, SK Hynix management cited extended memory supply constraints and continued AI-driven demand growth—read-through positive for MU. One analyst noted that pricing stability and customer deal longevity matter more than margin maximization in memory.

bullets.title: Iran-US escalation: oil spikes 3.4% to $82 WTI before reversing; geopolitical risk elevated into Fed day
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC launched ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan at 5:45pm ET; the US military reported all were successfully intercepted. WTI surged 3.4% to ~$82 on the news before giving back gains as Saudi Arabia coordinated with CENTCOM and Iran denied escalation intent. Iran also seized three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. This geopolitical overhang compounds uncertainty into Wednesday's FOMC decision.

bullets.title: Korea KOSPI circuit breaker triggered twice; worst month on record feared
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell as much as 12.6% over two consecutive sessions, triggering circuit breakers both days and putting the index on track for its largest two-day and monthly declines on record (~35% down for July). Technical deleveraging was cited as the primary driver. South Korea's finance minister called an emergency market meeting and apologized for introducing leveraged ETFs. BoE is also probing Asian equity risk concentration at prime brokers.
